title: Congress.gov API (Library of Congress) with House and Senate roll-call votes
agency: Library of Congress (Congress.gov); Clerk of the House; Secretary of the Senate
questions: how did each party vote on a bill
how many bills became law in each Congress
cosponsors of a bill by party
status and actions of a bill

key_only: more than about 10 Congress.gov requests an hour (DEMO_KEY limit); roll-call XML needs no key

manual.how: Open each link in INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser and save the file under the given name: Congress.gov links carry the public DEMO_KEY (about 10 requests an hour; put your own api.data.gov key in its place for more), roll-call links are the official XML files at clerk.house.gov/evs/<year>/roll<NNN>.xml and www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/. On congress.gov, a bill's page (Actions, Cosponsors tabs) and search results can also be downloaded; upload the files.

cache.why: Bill status, actions and cosponsors change daily while Congress sits; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: Legislative data from Congress.gov, the House Clerk and the Senate are U.S. government works without copyright (17 U.S.C. 105); the Library of Congress asks for attribution. CRS report texts are public; Congress.gov's terms allow reuse of its data.

citation: Library of Congress, Congress.gov API, {dataset}, api.congress.gov (roll-call votes: Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which Congress (two-year term) or session? Default: the current Congress.
Which vote on a bill: final passage, cloture, a motion or an amendment? A bill often has several recorded votes; default: final passage in each chamber.
Bills only (hr, s) or resolutions too? Joint resolutions can become law; simple and concurrent resolutions cannot.
